column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Designed for third and fourth-year Bachelor of Technology students, the course matters because it equips future software engineers with practical capabilities to build and evaluate agent-assisted systems. Upon completing the course, students will be able to implement developer workflows integrating AI-assisted coding tools and coding agents, configure agent skills and Model Context Protocol servers, construct executable specifications, analyze loop engineering and iterative development processes, and evaluate automated testing and reliability metrics. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions, emphasizing a workflow-oriented understanding through hands-on development and experimentation.

Course Code: Implement developer workflows integrating AI-assisted coding tools and coding agents, using provided coding agent environments, such that all public integration tests pass and no warnings are generated by the static analyzer.
column2: Configure agent skills, tool use mechanisms, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, given a software development task description, such as identifying at least three distinct context bottlenecks with supporting log evidence.
column3: Construct executable specifications and specification-driven development artifacts, using requirement documents and schema templates, justifying each requirement mapping against at least one stated system constraint.
column4: Analyze loop engineering and iterative development processes, given a recorded software factory execution trace, identifying at least two control loop failures responsible for code generation degradation.
column5: Evaluate automated testing, evaluation harnesses, and reliability metrics, using a deployed AI-assisted software system, demonstrating live with three scenario walkthroughs chosen by the evaluator.
